# ML Training Demo Lab

Learn when to train a model, when a simpler method is enough, and how to tell the difference.

This repository is a hands-on tutorial built around eight ML use cases and a hybrid assistant capstone. You will train small models, inspect their failures, reload their saved artifacts, and compare quality with latency and operational complexity. Each lesson connects the underlying theory to runnable code and asks what would have to change before applying the technique in production.

The experiments include useful negative results. The distilled router reached 100% on generated test tickets but only 6/12 on independent challenges. Reinforcement learning changed weights without improving held-out accuracy. A reranker improved a controlled comparison yet hurt the best complete retrieval pipeline. Learning to interpret these outcomes is part of the curriculum.

## Start here

Read the [learning guide](docs/LEARNING_GUIDE.md) for prerequisites, evaluation vocabulary and the experiment workflow. Then choose a route:

- **Choosing an architecture:** use the [architecture decision guide](docs/ARCHITECTURE_DECISION_GUIDE.md) for use/avoid criteria, alternatives beyond the repo, and a reusable decision record.
- **Learning visually:** open the [nine Jupyter lessons](notebooks/README.md) for recorded-result charts, editable examples and architecture exercises. They run without model downloads and include saved figures for browsing.
- **First ML project:** start with D05, D06 and D07. These CPU lessons teach prediction, calibration, deployment measurement and explanations without downloading language models.
- **Language-model customization:** read the shared LoRA background, then work through D01, D02 and D04. Continue to D03 after producing the D02 checkpoint.
- **Search and assistants:** start with D08. After completing the component lessons, use D09 to investigate whether their gains survive integration.
- **Read before running:** each results document is a worked case study. Recorded results remain readable in a fresh clone even though the large local artifacts are not included.

## The lessons

| Lesson | Question you will investigate | Concepts and experiment | Read the observations |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [D01 · Distillation](docs/SLM_DEMOS.md#d01-distillation) | Can a small model imitate a larger model on a bounded task? | Teacher-label curation, supervised fine-tuning, abstention, amortization | [Language-model results](docs/SLM_RESULTS.md) |
| [D02 · Structured output](docs/SLM_DEMOS.md#d02-strict-syntax-and-executable-semantics) | When is valid JSON still the wrong answer? | Typed query ASTs, executable checks, compositional generalization, parser baseline | [Language-model results](docs/SLM_RESULTS.md) |
| [D03 · Verifiable rewards](docs/RLVR_DEMO.md) | Does reinforcement learning add anything after SFT? | GRPO, reward contrast, hidden evaluation, compute controls, best-of-N | [RLVR results](docs/RLVR_RESULTS.md) |
| [D04 · Local inference](docs/SLM_DEMOS.md#d04-local-model-and-simulated-device) | What do quantization and offline execution actually guarantee? | Adapter fusion, 4-bit export, device-command validation, simulator state | [Language-model results](docs/SLM_RESULTS.md) |
| [D05 · Tabular prediction](docs/CPU_DEMOS.md#d05-learn-a-tabular-risk-function) | Can a useful ranking still produce too many false alarms? | Logistic regression, boosted trees, temporal splits, calibration, drift | [CPU results](docs/CPU_RESULTS.md) |
| [D06 · Fast classification](docs/CPU_DEMOS.md#d06-export-and-time-a-request-classifier) | How much of service latency belongs to the model? | ONNX export, numerical parity, batching, warm versus startup timing | [CPU results](docs/CPU_RESULTS.md) |
| [D07 · Explanations](docs/CPU_DEMOS.md#d07-inspect-and-change-an-explanation) | What does a feature contribution explain? | SHAP, log-odds, background data, correlated features, sensitivity | [CPU results](docs/CPU_RESULTS.md) |
| [D08 · Retrieval](docs/RETRIEVAL_DEMO.md) | Should you tune the retriever, add a reranker, or do both? | Bi-encoders, cross-encoders, hard negatives, candidate recall, ablations | [Retrieval results](docs/RETRIEVAL_RESULTS.md) |
| [D09 · Hybrid capstone](docs/HYBRID_DEMO.md) | Does a better component make a better system? | Routing, fallback, external gates, end-to-end evaluation, changing knowledge | [Hybrid results](docs/HYBRID_RESULTS.md) |

Every tutorial includes concepts, an implementation walkthrough, observations to inspect, production tradeoffs, and exercises with interpretation guidance. The [architecture decision guide](docs/ARCHITECTURE_DECISION_GUIDE.md) helps you choose an approach; the [production tradeoff guide](docs/PRODUCTION_TRADEOFFS.md) develops its operating consequences.

## Run your first experiment

Run commands from the repository root with Python 3.12 and `uv` installed. On macOS, install OpenMP for XGBoost with `brew install libomp`. Start with the CPU environment:

~~~bash
uv sync --frozen
source .venv/bin/activate
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1
ml-demo doctor
ml-demo verify all --profile smoke
ml-demo train tabular --profile smoke --seed 41
ml-demo report all
~~~

The verification command runs the contract suite; it does not train every model. The small smoke training run checks the workflow. Its metrics are not the full experiment. Open the new run's `report.md` and compare the dummy, logistic and tree models. Then follow the [CPU tutorial](docs/CPU_DEMOS.md) to run the 50,000-event experiment and explain a prediction.

Training prints a unique directory. Replace placeholders such as `artifacts/tabular/<run>` with that printed path:

~~~bash
ml-demo evaluate tabular --run-dir artifacts/tabular/<run>
ml-demo verify tabular --run-dir artifacts/tabular/<run>
~~~

`evaluate` recomputes saved-model metrics; `verify --run-dir` checks file hashes. They answer different questions. The [reproduction guide](docs/REPRODUCTION.md) explains how to create the separate environments, download pinned models and replay the full lab.

## Explore interactively

The [local comparison UI](docs/COMPARISON_UI.md) turns the saved artifacts into an experiment viewer. Compare baselines, inspect individual failures, try a fresh language-model request, or edit a tabular feature and recompute its explanation.

The UI needs locally generated runs. A fresh clone contains source, tests, small challenge fixtures and dependency locks; it does not include model checkpoints, generated datasets or virtual environments. Links into `artifacts/` in results documents refer to the original local evidence bundle and do not resolve in a fresh clone. Reproduction creates new run directory names; use the paths printed by your commands to inspect your own evidence.

## What the lab establishes

The recorded implementation trained models for seven use cases, recomputed explanations from the saved D05 model for D07, and completed artifact reload and inference replay across all eight tracks. It also ran 320 executions of the ten capstone variants. The post-review validation passed 94 contract tests and seven fresh UI submissions. These records describe the implementation as evaluated on October 26, 2026; they are not a promise that a new machine will reproduce timing or accuracy exactly.

Most data is synthetic. Neural experiments use one training seed; the cheap CPU experiments use three. The observed host was an Apple M2 Max with 96 GB RAM. The MLX lessons require Apple Silicon/Metal in the supplied implementation. CPU lessons provide the smallest starting point; no claim is made that 96 GB is a minimum requirement for every lesson. Physical devices and customer systems are not connected.

Use the [final report](docs/FINAL_REPORT.md) as a synthesis of what was learned. The [implementation plan](docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md), [progress record](docs/PROGRESS.md), [conformance map](docs/CONFORMANCE.md) and [code-review case study](docs/CODE_REVIEW.md) explain how the evidence was built and checked.

The scope originated in the supplied six-page PDF **Fine-Tuning and ML Use Cases - Google Gemini**. Its examples supplied questions to test. Its embedded prompts were treated as source material, and its illustrative performance claims were not adopted as measured facts.

     3	import numpy as np
     4	from sklearn.metrics import average_precision_score, brier_score_loss, roc_auc_score, roc_curve

     6	
     7	def threshold_at_fpr(y, scores, budget: float = .05) -> float:
     8	    if len(np.unique(y)) != 2:
     9	        raise ValueError("Threshold selection requires both classes")
    10	    fpr, tpr, thresholds = roc_curve(y, scores)
    11	    allowed = np.flatnonzero(fpr <= budget)
    12	    best = allowed[np.argmax(tpr[allowed])]
    13	    # A threshold above 1 explicitly represents 'predict no positives'.
    14	    return float(thresholds[best]) if np.isfinite(thresholds[best]) else 1.000001

    17	def binary_metrics(y, scores, threshold: float) -> dict:
    18	    y = np.asarray(y)
    19	    scores = np.asarray(scores)
    20	    predicted = scores >= threshold
    21	    positive = y == 1
    22	    negative = ~positive
    23	    both = bool(positive.any() and negative.any())
    24	    return {
    25	        "rows": len(y), "positives": int(positive.sum()), "prevalence": float(y.mean()),
    26	        "pr_auc_average_precision": float(average_precision_score(y, scores)) if positive.any() else None,
    27	        "roc_auc": float(roc_auc_score(y, scores)) if both else None,
    28	        "brier": float(brier_score_loss(y, scores)), "threshold": threshold,
    29	        "recall": float(predicted[positive].mean()) if positive.any() else None,
    30	        "false_positive_rate": float(predicted[negative].mean()) if negative.any() else None,
    31	    }

    34	def bootstrap_ap(y, scores, seed: int, repetitions: int = 100) -> dict:
    35	    """Row bootstrap: descriptive only; correlated entities reduce independence."""
    36	    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    37	    values = []
    38	    for _ in range(repetitions):
    39	        ids = rng.integers(0, len(y), len(y))
    40	        if len(np.unique(y[ids])) == 2:
    41	            values.append(average_precision_score(y[ids], scores[ids]))
    42	    return {"lower": float(np.percentile(values, 2.5)), "upper": float(np.percentile(values, 97.5)),
    43	            "repetitions": repetitions, "method": "row bootstrap; ignores within-entity correlation"} if values else {"lower": None, "upper": None}

    20	def generate_events(n: int, seed: int) -> pl.DataFrame:
    21	    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    22	    timestamp = np.arange(n, dtype=np.int64) * 30
    23	    entity = rng.integers(0, 350, n)
    24	    # New entities in the final period provide an explicit unseen-entity slice.
    25	    new_mask = (np.arange(n) >= int(n * .8)) & (rng.random(n) < .25)
    26	    entity[new_mask] = rng.integers(350, 420, new_mask.sum())
    27	    susceptibility = rng.normal(0, .7, 420)  # latent; never enters the feature matrix
    28	    drift = np.arange(n) >= int(n * .8)
    29	    merchant = rng.choice(["grocery", "travel", "digital", "retail"], n)
    30	    amount = rng.lognormal(3.5 + .3 * drift, 1, n)
    31	    foreign = rng.binomial(1, .12 + .07 * drift, n)
    32	    failed = rng.poisson(.25 + .25 * drift, n)
    33	    age = rng.integers(1, 1800, n)
    34	    hour = (timestamp // 3600) % 24
    35	    # A stochastic outcome, with interactions and unobserved entity variation.
    36	    logit = (-4.8 + .65 * (np.log1p(amount) - 3.5) + .8 * foreign + .55 * failed
    37	             + 1.25 * (foreign * (merchant == "digital")) + .8 * (age < 45)
    38	             + .65 * ((hour < 5) & (failed > 0)) + susceptibility[entity]
    39	             + .7 * drift * (merchant == "travel"))
    40	    label = rng.binomial(1, 1 / (1 + np.exp(-logit)))
    41	    amount_missing = rng.random(n) < .025
    42	    observed_amount = [None if missing else float(a) for a, missing in zip(amount, amount_missing)]
    43	    return pl.DataFrame({
    44	        "event_id": np.arange(n), "timestamp": timestamp, "entity_id": entity,
    45	        "amount": observed_amount, "merchant": merchant, "failed_auth": failed,

    50	def build_features(events: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    51	    """Only strictly earlier events in the previous hour may influence a row.
    52	
    53	    Labels are never consulted. Events at the same timestamp do not influence
    54	    one another. The deque stores observed metadata, not delayed outcomes.
    55	    """

    57	        raise ValueError("Duplicate event IDs")
    58	    events = events.sort(["timestamp", "event_id"])
    59	    histories = defaultdict(deque)
    60	    rolling = []
    61	    for row in events.iter_rows(named=True):
    62	        history = histories[row["entity_id"]]
    63	        now = row["timestamp"]
    64	        while history and history[0][0] < now - 3600:
    65	            history.popleft()
    66	        prior = [item for item in history if item[0] < now]
    67	        amounts = [a for _, a, _ in prior if a is not None]
    68	        rolling.append((len(prior), sum(f > 0 for _, _, f in prior) / len(prior) if prior else 0,
    69	                        float(np.mean(amounts)) if amounts else None))
    70	        history.append((now, row["amount"], row["failed_auth"]))

    30	def generate(n, seed):
    31	    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    32	    drift = np.arange(n) >= int(n * .8)
    33	    rate = rng.lognormal(2 + .3 * drift, 1, n)
    34	    failure = rng.beta(.6, 4, n)
    35	    payload = rng.lognormal(2, 1.2, n)
    36	    paths = rng.poisson(4, n)
    37	    age = rng.uniform(0, 1000, n)
    38	    foreign = rng.binomial(1, .15, n)

    40	    prior = rate * rng.uniform(.3, 1.3, n)

    42	             + .8 * (age < 30) + .25 * drift * entropy)

    44	    x = np.column_stack([rate, failure, payload, paths, age, foreign, entropy, prior]).astype(np.float32)

    36	def explain_rows(tree, explainer, names, rows):

    39	    values = np.asarray(explainer.shap_values(transformed))

    41	    margin = tree.pipeline.named_steps["model"].predict(transformed, output_margin=True)

    52	            "calibrated_probability": float(calibrated[i]), "uncalibrated_probability": float(raw[i]),
    53	            "raw_log_odds": float(margin[i]), "base_log_odds": base,
    54	            "reconstruction_abs_error": float(residual[i]),
    55	            "contributions_log_odds": dict(zip(names, values[i].tolist())),
    56	            "reasons": [f"{names[j]} {'increases' if values[i,j] >= 0 else 'decreases'} raw model log-odds by {abs(values[i,j]):.4f} relative to the background" for j in order[:3]],

     8	def run_isolated(command, *, cwd, env, timeout):
     9	    """Capture a POSIX command; terminate its whole process group on interruption."""
    10	    with subprocess.Popen(command, cwd=cwd, env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
    11	                          stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, start_new_session=True) as process:
    12	        try:
    13	            stdout, stderr = process.communicate(timeout=timeout)
    14	        except BaseException as error:
    15	            try:
    16	                os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
    17	            except ProcessLookupError:
    18	                pass
    19	            stdout, stderr = process.communicate()
    20	            if isinstance(error, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
    21	                error.output, error.stderr = stdout, stderr
    22	            raise
    23	        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(command, process.returncode, stdout, stderr)

VALUES = {"priority": ["low", "normal", "urgent"], "status": ["open", "pending", "closed"],

OP_WORDS = {"eq": "equals", "ne": "does not equal", "gt": "is greater than", "ge": "is at least", "lt": "is less than", "le": "is at most"}
KNOWN_PAIRS = [("status", "age_hours"), ("team", "amount"), ("priority", "age_hours")]

def predicate(rng, field):
    if field in VALUES:
        return {"field": field, "op": rng.choice(["eq", "ne"]), "value": rng.choice(VALUES[field])}
    return {"field": field, "op": rng.choice(["gt", "ge", "lt", "le"]), "value": rng.randint(3, 97)}


def condition_text(node):
    if "all" in node or "any" in node:
        key = "all" if "all" in node else "any"
        return (" AND " if key == "all" else " OR ").join(condition_text(n) for n in node[key])
    return f"{node['field']} {OP_WORDS[node['op']]} {node['value']}"


def task_text(ast, style):
    aggregate = ast["aggregate"]
    op = aggregate["op"]
    verbs = {
        "count": ["Count tickets", "Return the number of tickets", "How many tickets are there", "Find the count of tickets"],
        "ids": ["List ticket IDs", "Return ticket IDs", "Which ticket IDs apply", "Find ticket IDs"],
        "sum": [f"Sum {aggregate.get('field')}", f"Return the total {aggregate.get('field')}", f"Calculate total {aggregate.get('field')}", f"Find the sum of {aggregate.get('field')}"],
        "mean": [f"Average {aggregate.get('field')}", f"Return the mean {aggregate.get('field')}", f"Calculate average {aggregate.get('field')}", f"Find the mean of {aggregate.get('field')}"],
    }
    return f"{verbs[op][style]} where {condition_text(ast['filter'])}."


def build(profile, seed):
    rows = []
    sizes = {"train": 1000, "validation": 100, "test": 160} if profile == "local" else {"train": 24, "validation": 8, "test": 8}
    for split_index, (split, count) in enumerate(sizes.items()):
        rng = random.Random(seed + split_index * 10000)
        for i in range(count):
            novel = split == "test" and i >= count * .75
            if novel:
                fields = rng.choice(NOVEL_PAIRS)
            elif i % 2:
                fields = rng.choice(KNOWN_PAIRS)
            else:
                fields = [rng.choice(list(VALUES) + ["age_hours", "amount"])]
            predicates = [predicate(rng, field) for field in fields]
            condition = predicates[0] if len(predicates) == 1 else {rng.choice(["all", "any"]): predicates}
            aggregate = {"op": rng.choice(["count", "ids", "sum", "mean"])}
            if aggregate["op"] in ["sum", "mean"]:
                aggregate["field"] = rng.choice(["age_hours", "amount"])
            ast = {"filter": condition, "aggregate": aggregate}
            style = rng.choice([0, 1]) if split == "train" else 2 if split == "validation" else 3
            rows.append({"id": f"{split}-{i}", "split": split, "family": f"phrasing-{style}",
                         "novel_composition": novel, "system": SYSTEM,

                         "expected": ast, "answer": json.dumps(ast, separators=(",", ":")),
                         "fixture_seed": seed * 100000 + split_index * 10000 + i})
    return rows

    def walk(node):

399	SYSTEM = (
400	    'Return only compact JSON with exactly filter and aggregate, no markdown. '
401	    'A filter is {"field":FIELD,"op":OP,"value":VALUE}, {"all":[FILTERS]}, or {"any":[FILTERS]}. '
402	    'Fields: priority (low,normal,urgent), status (open,pending,closed), team (billing,support,security), '
403	    'age_hours and amount (numbers). Operators: eq,ne; numbers also gt,ge,lt,le. '
404	    'Aggregate: {"op":"count"}, {"op":"ids"}, or {"op":"sum"|"mean","field":"age_hours"|"amount"}. '
405	    'Use all for AND and any for OR. Interpret the request; do not execute code.'
406	)
407	VALUES = {"priority": ["low", "normal", "urgent"], "status": ["open", "pending", "closed"],
408	          "team": ["billing", "support", "security"]}
409	OP_WORDS = {"eq": "equals", "ne": "does not equal", "gt": "is greater than", "ge": "is at least", "lt": "is less than", "le": "is at most"}
410	KNOWN_PAIRS = [("status", "age_hours"), ("team", "amount"), ("priority", "age_hours")]
411	NOVEL_PAIRS = [("priority", "amount"), ("status", "team")]

414	def predicate(rng, field):
415	    if field in VALUES:
416	        return {"field": field, "op": rng.choice(["eq", "ne"]), "value": rng.choice(VALUES[field])}
417	    return {"field": field, "op": rng.choice(["gt", "ge", "lt", "le"]), "value": rng.randint(3, 97)}
418

420	def condition_text(node):
421	    if "all" in node or "any" in node:
422	        key = "all" if "all" in node else "any"
423	        return (" AND " if key == "all" else " OR ").join(condition_text(n) for n in node[key])
424	    return f"{node['field']} {OP_WORDS[node['op']]} {node['value']}"

427	def task_text(ast, style):
428	    aggregate = ast["aggregate"]
429	    op = aggregate["op"]
430	    verbs = {
431	        "count": ["Count tickets", "Return the number of tickets", "How many tickets are there", "Find the count of tickets"],
432	        "ids": ["List ticket IDs", "Return ticket IDs", "Which ticket IDs apply", "Find ticket IDs"],
433	        "sum": [f"Sum {aggregate.get('field')}", f"Return the total {aggregate.get('field')}", f"Calculate total {aggregate.get('field')}", f"Find the sum of {aggregate.get('field')}"],
434	        "mean": [f"Average {aggregate.get('field')}", f"Return the mean {aggregate.get('field')}", f"Calculate average {aggregate.get('field')}", f"Find the mean of {aggregate.get('field')}"],

439	def build(profile, seed):
440	    rows = []
441	    sizes = {"train": 1000, "validation": 100, "test": 160} if profile == "local" else {"train": 24, "validation": 8, "test": 8}

443	        rng = random.Random(seed + split_index * 10000)
444	        for i in range(count):

446	            if novel:

448	            elif i % 2:
449	                fields = rng.choice(KNOWN_PAIRS)
450	            else:

452	            predicates = [predicate(rng, field) for field in fields]
453	            condition = predicates[0] if len(predicates) == 1 else {rng.choice(["all", "any"]): predicates}
454	            aggregate = {"op": rng.choice(["count", "ids", "sum", "mean"])}
455	            if aggregate["op"] in ["sum", "mean"]:
456	                aggregate["field"] = rng.choice(["age_hours", "amount"])
457	            ast = {"filter": condition, "aggregate": aggregate}
458	            style = rng.choice([0, 1]) if split == "train" else 2 if split == "validation" else 3

462	                         "expected": ast, "answer": json.dumps(ast, separators=(",", ":")),
463	                         "fixture_seed": seed * 100000 + split_index * 10000 + i})

467	def tables(ast, seed, hidden=True):
468	    """Independent randomized tables plus boundary witnesses and empty input."""
469	    rng = random.Random(seed + (901337 if hidden else 0))
470	    def random_table():
471	        return [{"id": f"r{i}", "priority": rng.choice(VALUES["priority"]), "status": rng.choice(VALUES["status"]),
472	                 "team": rng.choice(VALUES["team"]), "age_hours": rng.randint(0, 110), "amount": rng.randint(0, 110)} for i in range(48)]
473	    thresholds = {"age_hours": [], "amount": []}
474	    def walk(node):
475	        if "all" in node or "any" in node:
476	            for child in node.get("all", node.get("any")):
477	                walk(child)
478	        elif node["field"] in thresholds:
479	            thresholds[node["field"]].append(node["value"])
480	    walk(ast["filter"])
481	    choices = {}
482	    for field, values in thresholds.items():
483	        # Dataset grammar has at most one predicate per numeric field.
484	        pivot = values[0] if values else 24
485	        choices[field] = sorted({0, max(0, pivot-1), pivot, pivot+1, 110})
486	    witness = []
487	    for i, values in enumerate(product(VALUES["priority"], VALUES["status"], VALUES["team"], choices["age_hours"], choices["amount"])):
488	        witness.append(dict(zip(["priority", "status", "team", "age_hours", "amount"], values)) | {"id": f"w{i}"})
489	    return [random_table(), witness, []]

492	def typed_slot(text):
493	    """A deterministic bounded-language parser; not constrained neural decoding."""
494	    lower = re.sub(r"\s+request reference [a-z0-9-]+\.\s*$", "", text.lower().strip())
495	    if lower.count(" where ") != 1:
496	        raise InvalidQuery("Outside typed-slot predicate grammar")
497	    head, condition = lower.split(" where ")
498	    if re.fullmatch(r"(?:list ticket ids|return ticket ids|which ticket ids apply|find ticket ids)", head):
499	        aggregate = {"op": "ids"}
500	    elif re.fullmatch(r"(?:count tickets|return the number of tickets|how many tickets are there|find the count of tickets)", head):
501	        aggregate = {"op": "count"}
502	    else:
503	        total = re.fullmatch(r"(?:sum(?: of)?|return the total|calculate total|find the sum of) (age_hours|amount)", head)
504	        mean = re.fullmatch(r"(?:average(?: of)?|return the mean|calculate average|find the mean of) (age_hours|amount)", head)
505	        if not total and not mean:
506	            raise InvalidQuery("Outside typed-slot aggregate grammar")
507	        aggregate = {"op":"sum" if total else "mean", "field":(total or mean)[1]}
508	    condition = condition.rstrip(". ")
509	    if " and " in condition and " or " in condition:
510	        raise InvalidQuery("Mixed precedence is not supported by this baseline")
511	    joiner = " and " if " and " in condition else " or " if " or " in condition else None
512	    parts = condition.split(joiner) if joiner else [condition]
513	    predicates = []
514	    words_to_op = {v: k for k, v in OP_WORDS.items()}
515	    for part in parts:
516	        match = re.fullmatch(r"(priority|status|team|age_hours|amount) (equals|does not equal|is greater than|is at least|is less than|is at most) ([a-z]+|[0-9]+)", part)
517	        if not match:
518	            raise InvalidQuery("Outside typed-slot predicate grammar")
519	        field, op, value = match.groups()
520	        predicates.append({"field": field, "op": words_to_op[op], "value": int(value) if field not in VALUES else value})
521	    condition_ast = {"all" if joiner == " and " else "any": predicates} if joiner else predicates[0]
522	    ast = {"filter": condition_ast, "aggregate": aggregate}
523	    validate(ast)
524	    return ast

    98	def train_sft_control(run, rows, seed, device, seconds):
    99	    """Same SFT initialization and adapter, matched by measured training wall time."""
   100	    model, tokenizer = models.load(run / "shared_sft", device, trainable=True, seed=seed)

   106	    order, losses, tokens = list(rows), [], 0
   107	    random.Random(seed).shuffle(order)
   108	    model.train()
   109	    start = time.perf_counter()
   110	    step = 0
   111	    while time.perf_counter() - start < seconds or step == 0:
   112	        examples = [order[(step*4+i) % len(order)] for i in range(4)]
   113	        sequences, labels = [], []
   114	        for row in examples:
   115	            prefix = tokenizer.encode(models.prompt(tokenizer, row), add_special_tokens=False)
   116	            target = tokenizer.encode(row["answer"], add_special_tokens=False) + [tokenizer.eos_token_id]

   118	                raise ValueError("SFT control exceeds sequence budget")
   119	            sequences.append(prefix+target)
   120	            labels.append([-100]*len(prefix)+target)
   121	            tokens += len(target)
   122	        length = max(map(len, sequences))
   123	        inputs = torch.tensor([s+[tokenizer.pad_token_id]*(length-len(s)) for s in sequences], device=device)
   124	        targets = torch.tensor([s+[-100]*(length-len(s)) for s in labels], device=device)
   125	        masks = torch.tensor([[1]*len(s)+[0]*(length-len(s)) for s in sequences], device=device)
   126	        loss = model(input_ids=inputs, attention_mask=masks, labels=targets).loss
   127	        loss.backward()
   128	        torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.)

   130	        optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
   131	        losses.append(float(loss.detach().cpu()))
   132	        step += 1
   133	        if step % 25 == 0:
   134	            print(f"SFT wall-time control step={step} loss={losses[-1]:.4f}", flush=True)

   136	    after = models.adapter_hash(model)
   137	    model.save_pretrained(run / "sft_control_adapter")
   138	    evidence = {"optimizer": "AdamW", "learning_rate": 2e-5, "learning_rate_schedule": "constant",
   139	                "weight_decay": 0., "max_grad_norm": 1., "batch_size": 4,
   140	                "optimizer_steps": step, "completion_tokens": tokens, "losses": losses,
   141	                "initial_adapter_sha256": before, "final_adapter_sha256": after, "parameters_changed": before != after,
   142	                "target_training_seconds": seconds, "elapsed_training_seconds": elapsed,

   146	    del model, tokenizer, optimizer
   147	    models.release()

321	   100	    model, tokenizer = models.load(run / "shared_sft", device, trainable=True, seed=seed)

333	   112	        examples = [order[(step*4+i) % len(order)] for i in range(4)]

class Worker:
    def __init__(self, kind, config, log_dir, clean=False):
        environment = {"language":"mlx", "retrieval":"transformers", "rlvr":"rlvr"}[kind]
        venv = ".venv-repro" if clean else ".venv"
        python = ROOT / f"environments/{environment}/{venv}/bin/python"
        self.log = (log_dir / f"{kind}.log").open("w")
        try:
            self.process = subprocess.Popen([str(python),"-m","ml_training.hybrid_workers",kind,str(config)],
                cwd=ROOT, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=self.log, text=True, bufsize=1,
                env=os.environ | {"HF_HUB_OFFLINE":"1","TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE":"1","TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM":"false"})
        except BaseException:
            self.log.close()
            raise
        self.selector = selectors.DefaultSelector()
        self.selector.register(self.process.stdout, selectors.EVENT_READ)

    def call(self, request):
        start = time.perf_counter()
        self.process.stdin.write(json.dumps(request)+"\n")
        self.process.stdin.flush()
        if not self.selector.select(timeout=180):
            raise TimeoutError("Local model worker did not answer within 180 seconds")
        line = self.process.stdout.readline()
        if not line:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Local worker exited: {self.process.poll()}; inspect its log")
        response = json.loads(line)
        if not response["ok"]:
            raise RuntimeError(response["error"])
        response["roundtrip_seconds"] = time.perf_counter()-start
        return response

    def close(self):
        try:
            if self.process.poll() is None:
                try:
                    self.process.stdin.write('{"task":"close"}\n')
                    self.process.stdin.flush()
                except (BrokenPipeError, OSError):
                    pass  # The child may have exited between poll and write.
                try:
                    self.process.wait(timeout=15)
                except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                    self.process.terminate()
                    try:
                        self.process.wait(timeout=15)
                    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                        self.process.kill()
                        self.process.wait()
        finally:
            self.selector.close()
            for stream in [self.process.stdin, self.process.stdout]:
                try:
                    stream.close()
                except OSError:
                    pass
            self.log.close()

content.text:
# Code and design review: ml-training demo lab

This repo is in better shape than most tutorial repos. Every run records its environment and file hashes, models and thresholds are chosen on validation data before the test set is opened, the query language runs through a bounded interpreter rather than `eval`, and failed experiments are written up instead of hidden. The CPU suite passes: 113 passed, 6 skipped. The problems are mostly cases where a report or measurement says something the code doesn't support. That matters more than usual here, because the repo's selling point is that its evidence can be trusted.

## Code review (most severe first)

**1. Every D06 report states the opposite of its own measurement.**
`src/ml_training/fast_classifier.py:212` always writes "The p95 model target is 1 ms; actual measurements are above." I checked all four local runs. Each one records `p95_target_met: True`, with ONNX p95 between 0.0045 and 0.0075 ms, and each `report.md` still contains the hard-coded sentence. `docs/CPU_RESULTS.md:51` correctly says both backends met the target, so the generated reports contradict the docs. The fix is to build that sentence from `benchmarks["onnx_batch_1"]["p95"]`.

**2. The ONNX fresh-process startup time mostly measures unrelated imports.**
`cold_infer.py:15` imports `session` from `fast_classifier`, which also pulls in sklearn, skl2onnx and polars. I measured `import onnxruntime` at 0.07 s and `import ml_training.fast_classifier` at 1.05 s. The recorded startup figures are 1.10–1.19 s, so about 90% is loading training libraries a deployed ONNX service wouldn't need. That undercuts the D06 lesson that startup costs more than HTTP. The fix is to move `session` and `probabilities` into a small module that imports only onnxruntime and numpy.

**3. D03's "hidden" evaluation reuses two of the three fixture tables from the training reward.**
In `schema_data.tables`, the `hidden` flag only changes the seed of the 48-row random table. The boundary-witness table and the empty table are the same ones the reward uses. So `public_pass_hidden_failure_rate`, the reward-hacking signal, can only catch an exploit that one random table happens to expose. `docs/RLVR_DEMO.md:66` is technically accurate but reads as stronger than this. The fix is to give the hidden set its own witnesses (different pivots) and several random tables.

**4. The D02 typed-slot baseline already knows the test-set wording.**
The regexes in `schema_data.typed_slot` cover all four phrasing styles, including style 2 (validation) and style 3 (test). The neural models never see style 3 during training. The "disjoint phrasing families" claim holds for the models but not for the baseline, so its test score is effectively in-distribution. The hybrid's `checked_query` then uses the same parser as an "independent" check. Either restrict the parser to the training styles or label this asymmetry in the D02 results.

**5. D01 "distillation" effectively trains on gold labels.**
`distillation.curate` accepts a teacher answer only when it exactly equals the oracle answer. So the student's training targets are the oracle labels, limited to the examples the teacher got right. The teacher acts as a filter: its mistakes and style never reach the student, and the student never sees the cases the teacher found hard. `SLM_DEMOS.md:44` calls this an "independent check". It's a legitimate design, but the lesson should state it plainly, because it changes what the D01 result shows.

**6. Smaller issues**
- `rlvr.py:79` writes `"trainer_version": "1.8.0"` as a fixed string. It should read `trl.__version__`, or the provenance record can drift from reality.
- Failure handling is inconsistent. The D01/D02/D03/D04 trainers mark failed runs `failed`. The D05/D06 trainers leave crashed runs stuck at `started`. `explainability.run` creates its run directory before checking `row_index`, so a bad index leaves an orphaned directory behind.
- `structured.benchmark` and `distillation.latency` report p95 and p99 from 12 samples, where p99 is effectively the maximum. In a lab that teaches measurement boundaries, report median and max, or take more samples.
- `prepare()` in every data module: if a run crashes after `mkdir` but before the manifest is written, every later call fails with `FileExistsError` until someone deletes the folder by hand.
- The CLI has three rough edges:
  - `ml-demo train` with no demo, and `train all`, both print "A demo is not implemented yet".
  - `verify tabular` without `--run-dir` silently runs the whole pytest suite.
  - `list` reports every demo as "implemented".
- In the D06 HTTP handler, deeply nested JSON raises a `RecursionError` that isn't caught, so the connection drops without a 400. This is a minor issue since the server is loopback only.

## Design review

**What works**
- The evidence model: run manifests, hash checks, choosing on validation before test, and the challenge fixtures.
- Negative results are treated as part of the curriculum.
- The bounded AST language is a good teaching device for "valid JSON is still the wrong answer".
- Runtime gates check model output before anything uses it, and the device simulator is deterministic.

**What I'd change**
1. **Write report claims from data, not by hand.** Finding 1 is the visible case of a wider pattern: each `write_report` mixes measured values with fixed prose. Any sentence that asserts a result should be computed from the run, or left out.
2. **Re-evaluation requires exact equality, which learners will hit.** `reevaluate` compares floats and generated text exactly. That's right for your own machine. A learner on a different Mac or library version will see "Re-evaluation mismatch" and can't tell a bug from numerical drift. Add a tolerance mode, plus an error message that separates "outputs drifted" from "artifact tampered".
3. **Split the learning docs from the project records.** `docs/` holds about 35k words. The tutorials are mixed with `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN`, `PROGRESS`, `CONFORMANCE`, `CODE_REVIEW` and `FINAL_REPORT`. Moving the records to `docs/project/` would make the learner path much clearer.
4. **Centralize the five-environment setup.** `rlvr.py:193` and `hybrid.Worker` hard-code paths like `environments/<env>/.venv/bin/python`. Put the environment-to-interpreter mapping in `configs/` and add one bootstrap script, so a missing environment fails with an actionable message instead of `FileNotFoundError`.
5. **D09 can't run from a fresh clone.** `hybrid.bindings` depends on `artifacts/validation/selected_*.json`, which comes from `scripts/select_component_runs.py`. That's documented in `REPRODUCTION.md`, but it's the steepest step in the curriculum. A `ml-demo prepare hybrid --auto-select` command would remove it.
6. **Replace the CLI's if/elif chain with a registry.** The 170-line branch in `cli.py` should map each demo to its prepare, train, evaluate and infer handlers. That removes the misleading errors above and makes new lessons cheap to add.
7. **Add a formatter.** Formatting is inconsistent: `hybrid.py`, `explainability.infer_edit` and the UI use a dense no-space-after-comma style unlike the rest. Adding ruff with `ruff format` in the pre-test step would fix it.

I can fix findings 1, 2 and 6 now; they're small and mechanical. Findings 3–5 change the experiments, so they'd need re-runs and doc updates, and those are your call. I can also turn this review into a shareable page if you want.

"""Record explicit hybrid components and optional additional CPU replication runs."""

import argparse
from pathlib import Path

from ml_training.common import ROOT, digest, read_json, verify_run, write_json

DEMOS = ["distillation","schema_dsl","rlvr","edge","tabular","fast_classifier","explainability","retrieval"]
EXTRA_CPU = {f"{demo}-{seed}":(demo,seed) for demo in ["tabular","fast_classifier"] for seed in [42,43]}


def select_runs(paths, additional_cpu=None):
    paths = {demo:Path(path).resolve() for demo,path in paths.items()}
    if set(paths) != set(DEMOS):
        raise ValueError("Select all eight demo components")
    additional_cpu = {key:Path(path).resolve() for key,path in (additional_cpu or {}).items()}
    if set(additional_cpu) - set(EXTRA_CPU):
        raise ValueError("Additional CPU runs must be tabular/classifier seeds 42 or 43")
    def checked(path, demo, seed):
        verify_run(path)
        record = read_json(path / "run.json")
        if record["demo"]!=demo or record["profile"]!="local" or record["status"]!="evaluated" or record["seed"]!=seed:
            raise ValueError(f"Expected an evaluated local seed-{seed} {demo} run: {path}")
        path.relative_to(ROOT)
        return record
    info = {demo:checked(path,demo,41) for demo,path in paths.items()}
    for key,path in additional_cpu.items():
        checked(path,*EXTRA_CPU[key])
    if info["rlvr"]["source_manifest_sha256"]!=digest(paths["schema_dsl"] / "run.json"):
        raise ValueError("RLVR must have started from the selected schema/DSL checkpoint")
    if info["explainability"]["source_manifest_sha256"]!=digest(paths["tabular"] / "run.json"):
        raise ValueError("Explanation source must match the selected tabular run")
    destination = ROOT / "artifacts/validation"
    cpu_path, structured_path = destination / "selected_cpu_runs.json", destination / "selected_structured_runs.json"
    cpu = read_json(cpu_path) if cpu_path.exists() else {}
    structured = read_json(structured_path) if structured_path.exists() else {}
    for demo in ["tabular","fast_classifier","explainability"]:
        cpu[f"{demo}-41"] = str(paths[demo].relative_to(ROOT))
    cpu.update({key:str(path.relative_to(ROOT)) for key,path in additional_cpu.items()})
    for demo in ["schema_dsl","edge"]:
        structured.setdefault(demo,{})["local"] = str(paths[demo].relative_to(ROOT))
    for demo in ["distillation","retrieval","rlvr"]:
        write_json(destination / f"selected_{demo}_run.json",{"run":str(paths[demo].relative_to(ROOT))})
    write_json(cpu_path,cpu)
    write_json(structured_path,structured)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    for demo in DEMOS:
        parser.add_argument("--"+demo.replace("_","-"),type=Path,required=True)
    for key in EXTRA_CPU:
        parser.add_argument("--"+key.replace("_","-"),type=Path,
                            help="Include for the complete three-seed final audit")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    paths = {demo:getattr(args,demo) for demo in DEMOS}
    extra = {key:getattr(args,key.replace("-","_")) for key in EXTRA_CPU}
    select_runs(paths,{key:path for key,path in extra.items() if path is not None})
    print("Selected and verified all explicit component and CPU replication runs")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import sys

import pytest

from ml_training.common import digest, read_json, write_json
from scripts import select_component_runs as selection


def runs(root):
    def create(demo, seed):
        path = root / "artifacts" / demo / f"local-{seed}"
        path.mkdir(parents=True)
        (path / "model.bin").write_bytes(b"fixture weights")
        write_json(path / "run.json",{"demo":demo,"profile":"local","status":"evaluated","seed":seed,
                                     "files":{"model.bin":{"sha256":digest(path / "model.bin")}}})
        return path
    paths = {demo:create(demo,41) for demo in selection.DEMOS}
    for demo,source in [("rlvr","schema_dsl"),("explainability","tabular")]:
        record = read_json(paths[demo] / "run.json")
        write_json(paths[demo] / "run.json",record | {"source_manifest_sha256":digest(paths[source] / "run.json")})
    extra = {key:create(*value) for key,value in selection.EXTRA_CPU.items()}
    return paths,extra


def test_clean_checkout_cli_records_all_three_cpu_seeds(tmp_path,monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(selection,"ROOT",tmp_path)
    paths, extra = runs(tmp_path)
    args = ["select_component_runs.py"]
    for key,path in paths.items() | extra.items():
        args.extend(["--"+key.replace("_","-"),str(path)])
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys,"argv",args)
    selection.main()
    cpu = read_json(tmp_path / "artifacts/validation/selected_cpu_runs.json")
    assert set(cpu) == {"tabular-41","fast_classifier-41","explainability-41",*extra}
    assert all((tmp_path / path / "run.json").is_file() for path in cpu.values())


def test_wrong_replication_seed_cannot_partially_replace_selectors(tmp_path,monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(selection,"ROOT",tmp_path)
    paths,extra = runs(tmp_path)
    extra["fast_classifier-42"] = extra["fast_classifier-43"]
    with pytest.raises(ValueError,match="seed-42"):
        selection.select_runs(paths,extra)
    assert not (tmp_path / "artifacts/validation").exists()

# Reproducing the local demo lab

Reproducibility is itself a lesson: can another environment reconstruct the result, and which parts of the original conditions does that actually test? Start with the [learning guide](LEARNING_GUIDE.md) and one component tutorial before attempting the complete evidence bundle.

## Choose the strength of the check

| Check | What you learn | What it does not establish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Contract tests | Specified data, parser, gate and artifact invariants hold on the tested fixtures | Model quality |
| Visual notebook execution | Charts and small examples run from the versioned evidence snapshot without model artifacts | New training, new model inference or production performance |
| Smoke training | The small workflow can create and reload an artifact | Full-budget effectiveness |
| Artifact hash verification | Recorded files have not changed | Correctness or trustworthy provenance by itself |
| Saved-model replay | The installed environment reproduces recorded inference and metrics | A new training run will converge to the same model |
| Independent retraining | Training variability under the chosen seeds/settings | Transfer to new populations or hardware |
| Target deployment experiment | Behavior under specified real constraints | Reliability outside the evaluated conditions |

The recorded lab completed tests and saved-model replays; neural independent retraining and production deployment remain follow-up work. Reproduction commands below can perform substantial computation. Read the relevant tutorial's workload and hardware notes first.

## Recorded environment and scope

The observed host is an Apple M2 Max with 96 GB RAM, macOS arm64 and Python 3.12.13. The completed checks use a second installation of each relevant environment from its lockfile. They reload saved artifacts and regenerate outputs. They are not independent retraining replications, clean operating-system installs, cold filesystem-cache tests or cross-hardware benchmarks. All required replay and profile checks passed; [PROGRESS.md](PROGRESS.md) and [CONFORMANCE.md](CONFORMANCE.md) record the evidence.

## Install separate environments

The [visual notebooks](../notebooks/README.md) have an independent, lightweight environment: `uv sync --project environments/notebooks --frozen`. They do not require the model environments or macOS OpenMP below.

For the full lab, install `uv`, Python 3.12 and macOS OpenMP (`brew install libomp`) if absent. Training and UI dependencies are pinned in the root and four environment lockfiles; notebooks have a fifth environment lockfile. Do not combine their current Transformers requirements into one environment.

```bash
uv sync --frozen
uv sync --project environments/transformers --frozen
uv sync --project environments/mlx --frozen
uv sync --project environments/rlvr --frozen
uv sync --project environments/ui --frozen

UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv-repro uv sync --frozen
UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv-repro uv sync --project environments/transformers --frozen
UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv-repro uv sync --project environments/mlx --frozen
UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv-repro uv sync --project environments/rlvr --frozen
```

The relative `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT` is interpreted relative to each selected project. Confirm that the separate directories exist before running validators. The UI uses its own environment; model subprocesses use their corresponding task environment. Metal operations require GPU access; a restrictive process sandbox can make a usable host appear unsupported.

Download the exact model snapshots in [SLM_DEMOS.md](SLM_DEMOS.md) and [RETRIEVAL_DEMO.md](RETRIEVAL_DEMO.md), matching `configs/models.json`. `ML_DEMO_MODEL_CACHE` can override the Hugging Face cache root. After downloading:

```bash
export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false
.venv/bin/ml-demo doctor
.venv-repro/bin/ml-demo verify all --profile smoke
```

Offline flags prevent normal Hugging Face downloads but are not a network-isolation proof. D04 has a separate OS-enforced test below.

## Training from source versus replaying artifacts

A new checkout contains source, contracts and pinned environment definitions. Generated datasets, teacher cache, model artifacts and virtual environments are excluded from Git. Run the individual walkthroughs in dependency order to create them: D05/D06/D07, D08, D01/D02/D04, then D03 from the completed D02 run. Preserve the actual D01 teacher cache when continuing an interrupted experiment. Each training command prints its new run directory.

After creating all eight seed-41 local runs and the additional CPU runs, explicitly record the component selection. This helper verifies model hashes, task identity, seed, completed status and D02→D03 / D05→D07 source consistency before writing any selectors:

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/select_component_runs.py \
  --distillation artifacts/distillation/<run> \
  --schema-dsl artifacts/schema_dsl/<run> \
  --rlvr artifacts/rlvr/<run> \
  --edge artifacts/edge/<run> \
  --tabular artifacts/tabular/<run> \
  --fast-classifier artifacts/fast_classifier/<run> \
  --explainability artifacts/explainability/<run> \
  --retrieval artifacts/retrieval/<run> \
  --tabular-42 artifacts/tabular/<seed-42-run> \
  --tabular-43 artifacts/tabular/<seed-43-run> \
  --fast-classifier-42 artifacts/fast_classifier/<seed-42-run> \
  --fast-classifier-43 artifacts/fast_classifier/<seed-43-run>
```

The four extra CPU flags are optional for a seed-41-only hybrid walkthrough, but required to build a complete final-audit selection from a fresh checkout. Existing selections for other seeds are preserved. The original development machine's local evidence bundle already has these selections under `artifacts/validation/selected_*.json`. Replaying it requires the referenced local artifacts and pinned cached base models. The hybrid's bindings contain absolute paths to this checkout; moving the bundle requires creating a new comparison with selectors for the new location. Do not silently edit an already hashed run's bindings.

## Replay the measured tracks

Use each walkthrough's exact command options. These are the validation entry points:

```bash
.venv-repro/bin/python scripts/validate_cpu.py --help
environments/transformers/.venv-repro/bin/python scripts/validate_retrieval.py --help
environments/mlx/.venv-repro/bin/python scripts/validate_slm.py --help
environments/rlvr/.venv-repro/bin/python scripts/validate_rlvr.py --help
```

CPU reproduction verifies all model artifacts, recomputes metrics and explanations, checks ONNX parity and sends real localhost HTTP requests. Retrieval replay checks all seven comparisons, rankings, candidate pools and parameter hashes. SLM replay regenerates every recorded test/challenge output for all variants, including the teacher, classical router, typed parser and quantized device model. RLVR replay regenerates both greedy and four-sample outputs for all four variants, requiring exact raw text and metrics.

```bash
environments/rlvr/.venv-repro/bin/python scripts/validate_rlvr.py \
  artifacts/rlvr/<run> --device cpu --output artifacts/validation/rlvr.json

environments/rlvr/.venv-repro/bin/python scripts/check_rlvr_selection.py

environments/rlvr/.venv-repro/bin/python scripts/profile_rlvr.py \
  artifacts/rlvr/<run> --output artifacts/validation/rlvr-performance.json

sandbox-exec -p '(version 1) (allow default) (deny network*)' \
  environments/mlx/.venv-repro/bin/python scripts/validate_edge_offline.py \
  artifacts/edge/<run> artifacts/validation/edge-offline.json
```

Run timing profiles without competing model work. CPU inference uses four PyTorch threads for RLVR; ONNX uses its own explicit single-thread configuration. Warm measurements and fresh-process startup remain separate. Fresh-process time includes startup/import/loading overhead and uncontrolled OS caches. The RLVR evaluator is much slower than its short training stage because it generates hundreds of candidates for each of four variants.

The final audit also checks the paired native/ONNX batch profile and the small-perturbation explanation study. Run these against the three selected D06 runs and selected D07 run, preserving the original artifacts:

```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 .venv-repro/bin/python scripts/profile_classifier_batches.py \
  artifacts/fast_classifier/<seed-41-run> artifacts/fast_classifier/<seed-42-run> \
  artifacts/fast_classifier/<seed-43-run> --output artifacts/validation/classifier-batches.json

.venv/bin/python scripts/validate_explanation_stability.py \
  artifacts/explainability/<run> --output artifacts/validation/explanation-stability.json
.venv-repro/bin/python scripts/validate_explanation_stability.py \
  artifacts/explainability/<run> --compare artifacts/validation/explanation-stability.json \
  --output artifacts/validation/explanation-stability-reproduced.json
```

"""Minimal ONNX inference path: imports only onnxruntime and numpy.

Kept separate from the training module so fresh-process startup measures what
a deployed scorer would load, not scikit-learn, skl2onnx or polars.
"""

import numpy as np
import onnxruntime as ort


def session(path):
    options = ort.SessionOptions()
    options.intra_op_num_threads = 1
    options.inter_op_num_threads = 1
    options.execution_mode = ort.ExecutionMode.ORT_SEQUENTIAL
    return ort.InferenceSession(str(path), sess_options=options, providers=["CPUExecutionProvider"])


def probabilities(runtime, x):
    return runtime.run(None, {"features": np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float32)})[1][:, 1]

import re, pathlib
# 1. Replace duplicated failure blocks with the shared helper.
pat = re.compile(r'(    except BaseException as error:\n)        (\w+) = read_json\(run / "run\.json"\)\n        \2\.update\(status="failed", ?error=f"\{type\(error\)\.__name__\}: \{error\}"\)\n        write_json\(run / "run\.json", ?\2\)\n(        raise\n)')
for name in ["distillation","structured","rlvr","retrieval","hybrid"]:
    p = pathlib.Path(f"{name}.py"); s = p.read_text()
    s, n = pat.subn(r'\1        mark_failed(run, error)\n\3', s)
    assert n == 1, (name, n)
    s = re.sub(r'(from ml_training\.common import \(?)', r'\1mark_failed, ', s, count=1)
    p.write_text(s)

# 2. Wrap CPU trainers: everything after new_run(...) up to the final `return <var>`.
def wrap(name, func, var):
    p = pathlib.Path(f"{name}.py"); lines = p.read_text().split("\n")
    start = next(i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l.startswith(f"def {func}("))
    create = next(i for i in range(start, len(lines)) if f"{var} = new_run(" in lines[i])
    end = next(i for i in range(create, len(lines)) if lines[i] == f"    return {var}")
    body = ["    " + l if l.strip() else l for l in lines[create+1:end]]
    lines[create+1:end] = ["    try:", *body, "    except BaseException as error:",
                           f"        mark_failed({var}, error)", "        raise"]
    s = "\n".join(lines)
    s = re.sub(r'(from ml_training\.common import \(?)', r'\1mark_failed, ', s, count=1)
    p.write_text(s)
wrap("tabular", "train", "run")
wrap("fast_classifier", "train", "run")
wrap("explainability", "run", "result")
EOF

"""Install the lab's locked environments listed in configs/environments.json.

Standard library only, so it runs before any environment exists:

    python3 scripts/bootstrap.py                 # every environment
    python3 scripts/bootstrap.py cpu notebooks   # only the ones you need
    python3 scripts/bootstrap.py --repro cpu mlx # second installation for replay checks
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def main():
    config = json.loads((ROOT / "configs" / "environments.json").read_text())["environments"]
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("names", nargs="*", choices=[[], *config], metavar="ENVIRONMENT",
                        help=f"Any of: {', '.join(config)}. Default: all.")
    parser.add_argument("--repro", action="store_true", help="Install into .venv-repro instead of .venv")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if shutil.which("uv") is None:
        raise SystemExit("uv is required: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/")
    names = args.names or list(config)
    environment = os.environ | ({"UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT": ".venv-repro"} if args.repro else {})
    for name in names:
        project = config[name]["project"]
        print(f"==> {name}: {config[name]['purpose']}", flush=True)
        command = ["uv", "sync", "--frozen"] + ([] if project == "." else ["--project", project])
        # A relative UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT resolves inside each selected project.
        if subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, env=environment).returncode:
            raise SystemExit(f"Installing {name} failed; the uv output above names the cause.")
    if sys.platform == "darwin" and "cpu" in names:
        print("XGBoost on macOS also needs OpenMP: brew install libomp")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

I've made all ten changes: code fixes 1, 2 and 6, plus design items 1–7. Nothing is committed yet. The contract tests pass (119 passed, 6 skipped, including 6 new tests) and ruff reports no errors.

**Code fixes**
- **D06 report text:** the "target met / not met" sentence is now built from the measured p95. A fresh smoke run's report correctly says the target was met.
- **ONNX startup:** inference moved to a small new module, `onnx_runtime.py`, that imports only onnxruntime and numpy. Fresh-process startup fell from about 1.1 s to 0.10 s. The three recorded figures in `CPU_RESULTS.md` are still the old, inflated ones; I added a note there saying so, and you'll need to retrain to replace them.
- **Smaller fixes:**
  - D03 now records the installed trl version instead of a hard-coded "1.8.0".
  - Every trainer now marks a crashed run as `failed`, through one shared helper.
  - D07 checks the row index and edits before creating a run directory, so bad input no longer leaves an empty one behind.
  - An interrupted `prepare` now tells you which folder to delete and why that's safe.
